name: Dumbbell Floor Press
summary: A pressing movement lying on the floor, where the ground limits the range of motion. It trains the chest and triceps without a bench and is friendly to the shoulders.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and bring your upper arms to the floor with elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Hold the dumbbells over your chest or just outside it with palms facing your feet or each other.
Keep your wrists straight and your shoulder blades pulled back.
execution: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your chest.
Squeeze your chest at the top without shrugging.
Lower slowly until the backs of your upper arms lightly touch the floor.
Pause for a moment without relaxing, then press again.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out wide: keep them about 45 degrees from your sides.
Dropping the arms onto the floor and bouncing: lower under control and pause briefly.
Letting the wrists bend back: stack the wrist over the forearm.
Arching the lower back to push more weight: keep feet flat and ribs down, and pick a lighter weight.

references.title: Dumbbell Floor Press: The RIGHT Way (Most People Do This Wrong)
